extension.title: Copilot Scheduler
config.showNotifications: Show notifications when tasks are executed
config.executionHistoryLimit: Number of recent execution history entries to keep per task (10–500)
config.language: UI language (applies to extension Webview/Tree UI; settings-description updates may require window reload)
config.timezone: Timezone for cron scheduling, the allowed time window and the daily execution counters (e.g., 'Asia/Tokyo'). Leave empty for system default.
config.chatSession: Default chat session behavior. Tasks can override this.
config.chatSession.new: Create new chat session for each execution (more isolated, usually slower)
config.chatSession.continue: Continue in existing chat session (usually faster)
config.skillTemplates: Which Agent Skills the task form offers to insert into a prompt as `/skill-name`. Skills are read from `.github/skills`, `.agents/skills` and `.claude/skills` in local workspace folders (trusted workspaces only) and from `~/.copilot/skills` (or `$COPILOT_HOME/skills`), `~/.agents/skills` and `~/.claude/skills`. A skill is listed only when its folder name, `name`, and the Agent Skills naming rules agree. A workspace skill hides a user skill with the same name; a name found twice at the same level is left out. Skills with `user-invocable: false` are never listed. The form has Local Skill and Global Skill options that list workspace skills and user skills respectively, and a toggle to show all skills.
config.skillTemplates.explicit: Only skills that run when invoked (`disable-model-invocation: true`) (default)
config.skillTemplates.off: Do not offer skills in the task form
config.sessionHarness: Which kind of chat session new runs start in. Applies only when a run starts a new chat session. `auto` leaves the choice to VS Code. `local` is experimental: it starts a Local chat session with the `workbench.action.chat.newLocalChat` command and does not send the task if that fails. Scheduler never changes your VS Code settings and cannot force a Copilot (Agent Host) session.
config.sessionHarness.auto: Use the session type VS Code chooses for new chats (default)
config.sessionHarness.local: Experimental: start a Local chat session for each new run
config.modelFallbackChain: Fallback model order for tasks that opt in to model fallback. When a task's selected model is not in the model list, the first entry that matches a listed model (by id, name or family; separators ignored) is used instead. HydraFusion is a routing tier of Auto in Agent Host sessions and is skipped unless the model list includes it. Detailed model options are not carried over. Whether the replacement is applied depends on the session type (not confirmed for Copilot Agent Host sessions). Set to an empty list to disable. Up to 5 entries.
config.autoModeDefault: Default value for new tasks' auto-mode hint (inserts an autonomous-execution instruction at the beginning of the runtime prompt). To automatically keep AI-applied edits, configure `#chat.editing.autoAcceptDelay#`. If the link does not open, search for chat.editing.autoAcceptDelay in Settings.
config.commandDelayFactor: Delay multiplier for Copilot command sequencing (0.1–2.0). Lower is faster but may reduce stability in some environments.
config.manualRunNextRunPolicy: How to compute next run after Run Now
config.manualRunNextRunPolicy.advance: Advance past an existing future next run; otherwise recalculate from the current time
config.manualRunNextRunPolicy.fromNow: Recalculate from current time (ignores existing future next run)
config.missedRunPolicy: How to handle tasks due before scheduler start or restart. Evaluated on the next scheduler check; tasks due after startup are unaffected.
config.missedRunPolicy.runOnce: Run each overdue task once, regardless of how many occurrences were missed
config.missedRunPolicy.skip: Skip overdue tasks without recording an execution; advance each schedule to its next future occurrence
config.maxConcurrentAutomaticRuns: Maximum concurrent automatic prompt dispatches in this window, including jitter (1–10). Does not wait for model response completion. Oldest due tasks are selected first on each check. Run Now is not limited. Changes apply on the next check without cancelling active dispatches.
config.jitterSeconds: Default max random delay in seconds before running a task (0 = off). Each task can override this.
config.maxDailyExecutions: Maximum scheduled executions per day across all tasks (0 = unlimited, 1–100). ⚠️ Unlimited may risk API rate-limiting.
config.minimumIntervalWarning: Show a warning when a cron interval is shorter than 30 minutes
config.globalPromptsPath: Custom path for global prompt templates. Default: VS Code's User/prompts folder (Windows: %APPDATA%/Code/User/prompts, macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/prompts, Linux: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/Code/User/prompts or ~/.config/Code/User/prompts)
config.globalAgentsPath: Custom path for global agent files (*.agent.md). Default: auto-detect VS Code's User/prompts folder plus ~/.copilot/agents (Windows: %USERPROFILE%/.copilot/agents). Setting this overrides the default discovery roots.
config.promptFileFallback: What to do when a task using a local or global prompt file cannot read that file at execution time. Inline prompts are never affected.
config.promptFileFallback.snapshot: Run the saved prompt snapshot (current behavior).
config.promptFileFallback.blockWhenResol: Block the run when the prompt file path resolves but the file cannot be read. Fall back to the snapshot when the path cannot be resolved at all (for example the workspace is not open).
config.promptFileFallback.blockAlways: Block the run whenever the latest prompt file cannot be read.
config.reportIssue: 🐛 Found a bug? [Report an issue on GitHub](https://github.com/aktsmm/vscode-copilot-scheduler/issues)
config.lmTools.enableWriteTools: Allow Copilot Chat / agent mode to create, update, delete, toggle and run scheduler tasks via language-model tools. When disabled, write tools remain visible but their invocations are blocked; read tools remain usable.
config.lmTools.confirmationMode: Controls the extension-provided custom confirmation messages for Copilot Chat language-model write tools. VS Code or Copilot Chat may still show a generic approval dialog.
config.lmTools.confirmationMode.always: Always show custom confirmation messages from the extension for create, update, delete, enable-disable, and run tools.
config.lmTools.confirmationMode.destruct: Show custom confirmation messages from the extension only for destructive operations such as delete.
config.lmTools.confirmationMode.minimal: Suppress all extension-provided custom confirmation messages. VS Code or Copilot Chat may still show generic approval.
tool.scheduler_query.modelDescription: Query Copilot Scheduler for task information without side effects. Set 'kind' to one of: 'list' (all tasks, optionally filtered by scope and enabled state; prompt bodies are omitted and only a short promptPreview is returned), 'get' (single task by id, including the full prompt), 'history' (recent execution history, optionally filtered by taskId; automatic runs include dueAt, retentionLimit/retentionScope report the per-task retention cap, and statusSemantics explains that success confirms prompt dispatch rather than model response completion), 'preview_cron' (next occurrences of a cron expression; returns times in the configured timezone), 'list_models' (available AI models with their ids and supported reasoning efforts), 'list_agents' (selectable agents), or 'list_skills' (Agent Skills a task prompt can run as '/<name> <arguments>'; skills marked explicitOnly run only when invoked). Always use this before making changes to confirm which task the user means, and use 'list_models' / 'list_agents' / 'list_skills' before setting a model, agent or skill instead of guessing a name. Never write a promptPreview back to a task; fetch the full prompt with 'get' first.
tool.scheduler_create_task.modelDescript: Use when the user asks to schedule, set up, register, or automate a recurring Copilot prompt/task. Create a new scheduled Copilot task. Requires: name, cronExpression, prompt, and scope ('global' or 'workspace'). Optional fields include promptSource ('inline' | 'local' | 'global') and promptPath when promptSource is local or global. To pin a specific AI model, first call scheduler_query with kind='list_models' and pass one of the returned ids as 'model'; an unknown id is rejected. Execution controls autoMode, jitterSeconds, maxExecutionsPerDay, allowedTimeStart and allowedTimeEnd can also be set. New tasks can be created disabled and enabled later via scheduler_set_task_enabled. Enabling a task requires the user to have accepted the first-time execution disclaimer.
tool.scheduler_update_task.modelDescript: Use when the user asks to change, edit, reschedule, or revise an existing scheduled Copilot task. Update fields of an existing task. Do NOT pass 'enabled' here – use scheduler_set_task_enabled instead (the tool will refuse the update otherwise). Missing fields keep their current value. Unknown fields inside 'updates' are rejected. To change the AI model, pass a 'model' id from scheduler_query kind='list_models', or an empty string to go back to the default model.
tool.scheduler_delete_task.modelDescript: Use when the user asks to delete, remove, or cancel an existing scheduled Copilot task. Delete a task by id. This is permanent and cannot be undone. The user will be shown the task name, scope and workspace in the confirmation dialog before the tool actually runs.
tool.scheduler_set_task_enabled.modelDes: Use when the user asks to enable, disable, pause, resume, turn on, or turn off an existing scheduled Copilot task. Enable or disable a task by id. Enabling requires the user to have accepted the first-time execution disclaimer in the Copilot Scheduler view.
tool.scheduler_run_task.modelDescription: Use when the user asks to run, execute, trigger, or test an existing scheduled Copilot task once right now. Use scheduler_query first to identify its id. Recurring tasks keep their enabled state; one-time tasks apply afterRun (disable or delete) and cannot run again without rescheduling. Enabled recurring tasks advance nextRun according to manualRunNextRunPolicy. Success means prompt dispatch, not model response completion. saveFailed means already dispatched: do not retry automatically. Cancellation is checked before execution starts; an in-flight dispatch cannot be undone. Workspace tasks must belong to the current workspace; otherwise open that workspace or use the Copilot Scheduler view.
